title: Preventing Galvanic Corrosion with Dielectric Unions
description: An educational guide explaining why copper and galvanized steel pipes must be isolated using dielectric fittings to prevent rapid corrosion and pipe failure.
image_prompt: A professional educational 3D sectional cutaway visual of a water supply pipe connection. In the visual center, a copper pipe transitions to a threaded galvanized steel pipe through a dielectric union. The cutaway clearly shows the interior construction of the dielectric union, including the internal rubber gasket and plastic insulating sleeve separating the brass tailpiece from the steel housing. Realistic metallic textures, smooth copper, textured zinc-coated galvanized steel, and clean water flow inside. Clean neutral grey studio backdrop with warm ambient lighting. Vertical 9:16 composition with open space at top and bottom for text overlays. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no artificial arrows or graphics.
visual_story: The visual focuses on the interior structure of a dielectric union joining copper and galvanized steel pipes. Viewers can see how the plastic insulating collar and rubber washer physically prevent direct contact between the two different metals while maintaining a watertight seal.

on_image_text.hook: Why Copper and Steel Pipes Should Never Touch Directly
on_image_text.explanation: Direct contact between copper and steel in water creates an electrical cell that rapidly corrodes the steel.
on_image_text.takeaway: Always install a dielectric fitting or brass spacer when connecting dissimilar supply metals.
